messages:
sunil: Heads-up — we had a burst of noisy GPU latency alerts in eu-west-1 this morning around 06:12 UTC. Lots of short p95 spikes on inference pods, many auto-resolved within ~90s but they caused pages for the oncall. :wave:

sunil: Root pattern looks like short-lived node eviction / network flaps hitting a single rack. Paging threshold is currently firing on cluster-wide p95 > 1200ms for 1m. That seems too sensitive for these transient rack blips.

maya: saw that, thanks. Are the alerts grouping by node/rack/cardinality? If not we'll end up paging for every transient rack.

leah: Current prometheus expr is basically: `max_over_time(container_cpu_p95[1m]) > 1.2` and the alert has `for: 1m`. No grouping labels other than cluster.

jamie: suggestion: move to a two-stage rule: 1) a high-sensitivity signal that creates a ticket (no page) for short bursts, 2) escalate to pager only if sustained across multiple racks or 3m. Keeps noise down but pages on real incidents.

sunil: proposed concrete changes attached below (quick draft):

sunil: PromQL for burst detection (ticket only):
```
increase(gpu_request_latency_p95_seconds[2m]) > 0.3
```
(creates an alert that fires fast but with `severity: ticket` and no paging route)

sunil: PromQL for page-worthy sustained impact:
```
count by(rack_id) (  
  (gpu_request_latency_p95_seconds > 1.2)  
) >= 3
```
AND combined with `for: 3m` and grouping on `region, rack_id, model_variant` so we only page when >=3 racks are affected or one rack is affected for >3m.

maya::+1: Can we also add an alert that checks high-cardinality fanout? i.e., if the alert is touching >50 different pod_ids in <5m then it's likely infra and should page immediately.

leah: good call. Something like:
```
count_over_time(pod_id[5m]) > 50
```
(not exact, will refine)

jamie: we should also use silencing windows for planned maintenance in eu-west-1 and map autoscaler churn tags so transient autoscaler-caused spikes don't page. We already have a label `cause=autoscaler` on those events — can be used to mute.

sunil: action items: 
- jamie: update prometheus rules to add burst->ticket and sustained->pager rules (ETA EOD)
- maya: add grouping labels + high-cardinality detector to alert manager routing (ETA tomorrow)
- leah: add a dashboard panel for burst vs sustained counts and a quick playbook note (short blurb)

ops-bot: sunil acknowledged the thread (reaction :white_check_mark:)

maya: one more: lower severity pages should include immediate links to the per-cluster Grafana panel and the last 15m of network interface drops to speed triage. We forget to include those links in the alert body.

leah: I'll add `runbook_url` and grafana links to the alert templates. Also adding a small snippet to the alert: `annotations: { runbook: <link>, grafana_panel: <link>, owner: infra-oncall }`

jamie: if we want to be extra clever later: feed the `bursty` metric into the autoscaler to avoid overreacting to short latency spikes (save cost). Not for this sprint though.

sunil: sounds good. If no objections I'll merge the draft rules after jamie/maya's updates. We will run a 2-week quieting experiment in eu-west-1 with these changes and measure reduction in pages vs missed incidents. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maya: sounds good to me. :thumbsup:

jamie: I'll put the PR up shortly and tag infra-oncall.

sunil: thanks all — will follow up after the experiment window with metrics (page count, mean time to acknowledge, missed-sla count).
